headline: Singapore's Prime Minister Lawrence Wong says the AI boom will end in a correction at some point, so his country must use it now to build skills and better jobs.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score; remarks confirmed by CNA, but he gives no forecast of timing.
importance_line: Singapore's workers and chip firms are most affected, and other economies leaning on AI demand may share the risk, but Wong says plainly that nobody knows when a correction will come or who will be hurt.
summary: CNA reports that Wong, who is also finance minister, told the Forbes Global CEO Conference on Thursday 8 Oct 2026 that "no boom is forever" and "at some point, there will be a correction", though nobody knows when or who will be hurt. He said Singapore gains through makers of memory and specialty chips such as GlobalFoundries and Micron, and called for international safeguards on powerful AI, "perhaps under the auspices of the United Nations", while admitting that will take time.
notes: Pool source Bloomberg blocked; read CNA, which reported the same event itself.
